name: Havilah
overview: Havilah is a male figure in the Bible identified as a son of Cush. Beyond this unique attribute, Scripture does not provide additional details about his tribe or other distinguishing notes. His mention is brief and primarily genealogical in nature.
namesAndTitles: The name Havilah appears as a proper name in Scripture without an explicit meaning provided. There are no titles or divine attributions connected to his name in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Havilah as a son of Cush, establishing his place within the genealogical lineage presented in Genesis. No further family relationships are detailed beyond this paternal connection.
scriptureSignificance: Havilah's significance lies in his role within the genealogical framework of Genesis 10:7, which traces the descendants of Cush. This lineage contributes to the broader biblical narrative of the nations and peoples descending from Noah's sons, underscoring God's sovereign ordering of human history. Though not elaborated upon, Havilah's mention anchors the continuity of these early biblical genealogies.
